high_level_description: Wordless Breton woodblock-print illustration: during a severe coastal storm that has severed the communication line, one stone-house node continues preparing a repair guide from locally stored tools and documents while a distant peer remains unreachable; forceful carved lines, flattened geometry, black, indigo and ochre, strictly no text or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A windswept Breton headland slopes toward a dark sea under heavy rain clouds. The near ground supports one sheltered stone workshop; across a narrow rocky inlet, a second smaller headland remains visibly separated. Natural daylight breaks through one high window inside the near room. Blank surfaces contain no inscriptions, numerals, signage, interface graphics, or directional marks.

elements.desc: Granite coastal workshop representing the local node, shown as one coherent building with a slate roof and a clean cutaway front. Thick walls shelter a dry single-room interior containing a shuttered window and a sturdy work surface. The doorway is closed against the storm, yet the room remains fully usable and visibly lit.

Local craftsperson with light-brown skin, dark wavy hair tied behind the neck, an indigo wool jacket, cream shirt, ochre trousers, and black boots. Seated securely inside the workshop, they calmly compare two blank repair diagrams and shape a small wooden replacement part despite the broken connection outside.

Compact hand-operated repair bench inside the workshop, built from dark oak with a fixed vise, shallow parts tray, hand drill, and one partially shaped wooden component. All tools are physically present and usable without a remote service; the bench has no screen, antenna, cable socket, printed label, or external control.

Closed local archive chest against the inner stone wall, made from ochre oak with indigo iron straps and three shallow drawers holding blank folded sheets, wooden templates, and a sealed tool roll. Its contents remain inside the near workshop and provide the stored material used by the seated craftsperson during the outage.

Single severed communication line spanning the inlet, formed from a thick braided cable with two blunt broken ends separated by open air. One end remains fixed to the near workshop exterior and the other to the distant headland; neither end enters the room, touches the bench, or forms a pointed directional shape.

Small distant peer workshop on the opposite headland, built from pale granite with a dark slate roof and one unlit window. It remains intact but inaccessible across the stormy inlet, providing a clear second node without dominating the functioning local workshop in the foreground.
